title: Assistant/Associate/Full Professor in Agricultural and Applied Economics

Job Summary:

The Department of Agricultural and Applied Economics at the
University of Wisconsin-Madison seeks applications for a full‑time,
9-month, open rank faculty position (tenured or tenure‑track). We
invite scholars with a Ph.D. in Economics, Agricultural Economics,
or Applied Economics whose research centers on U.S. energy
markets.

The position will contribute to a University-wide cohort of new
faculty specializing in either (1) the foundations of Western
thought or (2) free-market solutions to societal challenges. As
such, we seek candidates with a strong emphasis on free‑market
mechanisms, market liberalization, competition, and the role of
policy in shaping private-sector behavior. The ideal candidate will
demonstrate an outstanding research record or exceptional research
potential, a commitment to high-quality teaching, the capacity to
contribute to UW-Madison’s mission as a leading center for economic
research and public engagement, and to advance our University’s
commitment to intellectual diversity and healthy civil
discourse.

Key Job Responsibilities:

Research Responsibilities

The successful candidate is expected to develop and maintain a
rigorous, externally funded and visible research agenda that
advances understanding of U.S. energy markets and resources
including electricity, oil, natural gas, nuclear, solar, wind and
emerging energy technologies through the lens of market-based
frameworks. Relevant areas may include, but are not limited
to:

Market structure, competition, and deregulation in energy
industries,
Price formation, volatility, and investment incentives in
competitive energy markets,
The interaction between environmental/energy policy and market
behavior,
Private-sector innovation and entrepreneurial responses to
energy transitions,
Regional and national energy market integration and
transmission policy.

Teaching Responsibilities

Teaching duties will include undergraduate and graduate courses in
energy economics, natural resource economics, institutional
economics, and/or related fields aligned with the candidate’s
expertise. The successful candidate will supervise Ph.D.
dissertations; mentor students pursuing careers in academia,
government, and industry; and contribute to curriculum development
in areas connected to energy and environmental markets. Excellence
in teaching and a demonstrated commitment to inclusive and
effective instruction are expected.

Service and Engagement Responsibilities

The position includes service to the department, college, and
university appropriate to rank. The successful candidate is
expected to engage in outreach and policy discussions at the
regional or national level, fostering dialogue regarding the
operation, design, and performance of U.S. energy markets,
including the role of market mechanisms, market liberalization,
competition, and policy in shaping private-sector behavior.
Meaningful engagement with research centers, interdisciplinary
initiatives, or industry partners is welcomed.

Department:

Department of Agricultural and Applied Economics, College of
Agricultural and Life Sciences ( https://aae.wisc.edu/ )

Compensation:

Negotiable
ACADEMIC (9 months)

Required Qualifications:

Successful candidates will have a record of or demonstrate
potential for:

Research in energy and natural resource economics and policy
centering on U.S. energy markets, with a strong emphasis on
free‑market mechanisms, market liberalization, competition, and the
role of policy in shaping private-sector behavior.
Publishing in leading peer‑reviewed journals.
Securing competitive external funding.
Excellence in teaching and a demonstrated commitment to
inclusive and effective instruction.
Graduate student training/mentoring.
Commitment to academic service, public engagement,
interdisciplinary collaboration, and professional integrity.
Strong communication and collaboration skills.

Applicants at any rank are encouraged to apply. At the rank of
Associate or (full) Professor the selected candidate's
qualifications must be sufficient to meet the requirements for
tenure in the Department of Agricultural and Applied Economics, in
the College of Agricultural and Life Sciences at the University of
Wisconsin-Madison by the position start date.

All requirements must be met by position start date

Preferred Qualifications:

Preference will be given to candidates whose work uses empirical,
theoretical, or mixed-method approaches to evaluate how markets
allocate resources and foster innovation in the energy
sector.

Education:

Ph.D. in Economics, Agricultural Economics, or Applied Economics
required.

About the Department and Institution:

The Department of Agricultural and Applied Economics at UW–Madison
is internationally recognized for its research and teaching in
agricultural, environmental, community and development economics.
Faculty collaborate across disciplines to address complex global
and local challenges.

UW–Madison is located in Madison, Wisconsin—an innovative and
vibrant city frequently ranked among the best places to live in the
U.S. The university seeks to foster a collaborative and inclusive
environment for different viewpoints and values community
engagement.

How to Apply:

Apply online at "Jobs at UW" ( http://jobs.wisc.edu ). Applications must be
received through UW-Madison's online application system.

Applicants must upload the following information as a single PDF
document:

1) Cover letter detailing interest and relevant training/experience
for this position (1-page)

2) Curriculum vitae

3) Statements of:

Teaching and mentoring philosophy and experience (1-page
limit)
Research experience and interests with a description of current
and planned research (3-5 page limit).

In addition, applicants will be asked to secure three letters of
recommendation.

The deadline for assuring full consideration is November 2, 2026;
however, the position will remain open, and applications may be
considered until the position is filled.

Institutional Statement on Diversity:

Diversity is a source of strength, creativity, and innovation for
UW-Madison. We value the contributions of each person and respect
the profound ways their identity, culture, background, experience,
status, abilities, and opinion enrich the university community. We
commit ourselves to the pursuit of excellence in teaching,
research, outreach, and diversity as inextricably linked
goals.

The University of Wisconsin-Madison fulfills its public mission by
creating a welcoming and inclusive community for people from every
background - people who as students, faculty, and staff serve
Wisconsin and the world.

The University of Wisconsin-Madison is an Equal Opportunity
Employer.

Qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment
